preamble: Spirantization of the aspirated bilabial stop [pʰ] to the bilabial fricative [ɸ]: the aspiration phase turns into turbulent friction at the lips. Eastern Indo-Aryan shows it clearly. In Standard Bengali ফ /pʰ/ is commonly realized [ɸ~f], and in eastern dialects and Sylheti it has become a fricative outright. The Greek φ [pʰ] > [f] change is often said to have passed through [ɸ], but there is no direct evidence for that stage, so it belongs under pʰ > f.

examples.note: Standard Bengali /pʰ/ is phonetically realized either as aspirated [pʰ] or, commonly, as the fricative [ɸ~f]; eastern dialects consistently have the fricative where western-central dialects have the aspirated stop.
Sylheti voiceless labials have spirantized to the homorganic fricative (p, pʰ > ɸ), part of its general deaspiration and spirantization.
